biography:
Andy Chittenden, a name now whispered with a mix of admiration and apprehension in the British racing paddock, wasn't born into motorsport royalty. His father ran a small garage in rural Oxfordshire, more accustomed to servicing tractors than tuning race cars. Andy's passion ignited not on a grand prix circuit, but on the makeshift dirt tracks he and his mates carved out in the local woods, tearing around on souped-up scooters. One fateful day, a local racing team owner, nursing a broken-down classic, witnessed Andy's raw talent firsthand as he coaxed the sputtering engine back to life. Impressed, he offered Andy a spot in his junior karting team.

Andy quickly ascended the ranks, his flashy driving style and even flashier personality making him both a fan favorite and a target on the track. He secured a few regional karting championships, but his transition to single-seaters was hampered by a lack of funding and several unfortunate racing incidents. His career stalled until MCR S2000 took a gamble on his undeniable potential, recognizing the raw talent hidden beneath the bravado. 

His debut season with MCR S2000 was a rollercoaster. Moments of brilliance were often overshadowed by costly errors, but glimpses of genuine speed were undeniable. He's now in his second year with MCR, under immense pressure to translate his promise into consistent results. The spotlight is on, and Andy, ever the showman, seems to relish it.
drivingStyle: Chittenden's driving is a high-risk, high-reward spectacle. He's known for his aggressive overtaking maneuvers, often braking later and carrying more speed into corners than his competitors deem prudent. He has a knack for finding grip where others don't, allowing him to pull off seemingly impossible moves. While his tire management can be erratic, he possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his car in short bursts, making him a formidable qualifier and a dangerous opponent in wheel-to-wheel combat. He doesn't shy away from a challenge, thriving under pressure, and seems to revel in the chaos of a tightly contested race.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities. Isabelle views Andy's style as reckless and disrespectful, while Andy sees her as overly cautious and boring. Their on-track battles are always intense.

Marcus, a seasoned veteran, publicly criticized Andy's driving following a controversial incident at Silverstone. Andy retorted with a sarcastic jibe about Marcus's 'retirement home' driving style, igniting a simmering feud.

Both rose through the ranks together and were always neck and neck, leading to a natural competitive rivalry. Ben is more even tempered and sees Andy as a showoff which creates friction between the two.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of Union Jack socks, regardless of the weather.
Insists on listening to classic rock anthems at full volume on his headphones immediately before every race.
Has a habit of polishing his helmet visor obsessively, even when it's already spotless.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the limits and taking chances. If you're not on the edge, you're taking up too much space."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Brands Hatch Indy race in torrential rain. Starting from P10, he carved his way through the field with a series of daring overtakes, securing his first major victory in dramatic fashion.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2023 Snetterton 300 after a late braking error, costing him a potential championship-defining win.
